paragraphs: A baroque picture frame at 9,776 polygons, quads only, with the scrolled corners, the beaded inner lip and the carved outer edge. The vertex count matches the faces exactly at 9,776, which is the mark of a closed quad shell. Ornament this fine is geometry, because carving faked in a map falls apart at a raking angle.

Four maps at 4096 x 4096 carry the gold leaf, the darker recesses and the rubbed wear on the high points. Gilding is read by its wear, so the maps do the aging that the carving cannot. Non-overlapping UVs let the frame go from gold to painted white without a second model.

An ornate baroque frame shares the page at $12 for a lighter purchase. On sale since 2016, it has been bought forty-two times at $29. It fits gallery and salon interiors, period rooms, mirror mockups and still life work with a canvas.

A set of beetroot, with whole roots, their tapering tails and the cut stalk tops left on at the crown. Several roots rather than one means a crate or a market stall can be filled from a single file. A beet is read by its rough skin and the flat where it sat in the soil.

CheckMate Pro certification covers the proportions, which matters when the vegetables sit next to a hand. The roots are separate objects, so they can be piled, scattered or shown singly on a board. A set like this saves the worst part of food work: making the same vegetable look different five times.

No alternate builds sit on the page, so the whole set is one purchase. On sale since 2017, it has been bought forty-two times at $39. It fits market and kitchen scenes, recipe visuals, packaging for produce and still life photography.

A sleeping mask at 2,487 polygons, quads only, with the contoured eye panels, the nose notch and the elastic strap behind. The 2,594 vertices sit above the faces, which a soft curved shell needs to stay smooth. The strap is modeled, so the mask can be shown worn, pushed up or lying folded on a nightstand.

Twelve maps at 4096 x 4096 and 2048 x 2048 carry the satin sheen, the stitching and the piping at the edge. Satin is all about the highlight, which is why an object this small still gets twelve maps. Non-overlapping UVs mean an eyelash print can be added without touching the shell.

Five builds share the page, including folded masks and eyelash patterns at $29. Listed in 2019, the mask has been taken forty-two times at $34. It fits bedroom and travel scenes, spa visuals, airline stills and character dressing for sleep.

A two person bobsled at 22,224 polygons, with the cowl, the open cockpit, the push handles and the runners under the frame. The 21,664 vertices sit below the face count, which a smooth shell with few openings allows. The runners and the cowl are separate, so the sled can be shown on ice or on a stand.

One map at 4096 x 4096 carries the painted shell, the sponsor panels and the scratches along the sides. A single map works here because the sled is one continuous body with almost no small parts. Non-overlapping UVs mean a national livery can be printed on without new geometry.

Six builds share the page: two and four person sleds, generic and team liveries, each at $33. On sale since 2017, it has been bought forty-two times at $39. It fits winter sport scenes, broadcast graphics, olympic style visuals and games on a bobsled track.
